problem: Which of the following is the graph of  $y={(\frac{1}{12})}^{x}-4?$
worked_solution:
First we plot the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{12})}^{x}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/e2f13711ca62a8a4a698e23bdfe78caca6df44d88ded27b88c517219dffbb866.png)

Next, we shift this graph $4$ units down. 
The horizontal asymptote under such a transformation becomes $y=-4,$ the $y$-intercept becomes $(0,-3).$
The resulting graph of $y={(\frac{1}{12})}^{x}-4$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/dc7f93220ac18ac5671b7b41de141940ca5296139b836d56755fdccf6164ed26.png)
